title: Chronological retention harmonization & Evidence Assertion API
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Customers need reliable, auditable exports of prompts/responses/request logs/metrics that exactly reflect the retention rules in force at any point in time. Today we have per-route TTLs and ad-hoc evidence exports but no consistent, time-aligned mechanism to assert what data was retained or purged at a given moment. This makes compliance reviews and forensic investigations brittle and increases legal risk for regulated customers.

Goal: Deliver a coordinated retention model ("chronological harmonization") that ties TTLs across prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics to a single timeline anchor, plus an Evidence Assertion API that produces signed, time-bound evidence bundles and a machine-readable assertion describing retention state, provenance, and residency for exported artifacts. The feature must work across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and integrate with audit logs and KMS/HSM for signing.

Out of scope: Deep UI redesigns of the Console; long-term archival storage backends (we will export bundles that can be ingested by archival partners but not build an archive service here).
user_stories: As a compliance lead, I can request an evidence bundle for a tenant for a specified time window and receive a signed package that proves what prompts/responses and logs were retained and what was purged under applicable TTLs.
As an SRE, I can configure a retention anchor policy per-tenant or per-route that synchronizes TTLs for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics so that eviction is deterministic and auditable.
As a security auditor, I can call the Evidence Assertion API to get a manifest that includes hash-chained digests, KMS signature metadata, and data residency assertions for exported artifacts.
As a Product owner, I can preview 'retention state at time T' in the Console (read-only) to validate policies before running exports.
acceptance_criteria: API: Evidence Assertion API endpoint exists and returns a signed manifest (JSON) that lists included artifacts, their SHA-256 digests, retention-policy IDs, and whether the item was preserved or purged for the requested window.

Harmonization: TTL enforcement job consults per-route anchor and evicts/promotes items so that prompts/responses/logs/metrics align to the same chronology within +/- 1 minute determinism for eviction ordering.
Export: Evidence bundles (tar.gz) are buildable on demand and include a manifest, digests, and a detached KMS-backed signature; bundle size/latency SLOs documented for 30-day and 365-day windows.
Residency: Manifest contains region residency per-artifact and release channel (hosted/dedicated/private) metadata.
Audit: Every Evidence Assertion API call emits an immutable audit event with caller identity, time range, and exported object IDs; events are queryable in the Console's audit timeline.
QA: End-to-end tests that simulate TTL changes and verify manifest statements across retention-change timelines pass in CI.
tech_considerations: Retention anchor: implement lightweight per-route 'anchor timestamp' used by eviction and snapshot jobs. Anchors are logical; changes to anchors produce an audit event and require a short grace window before enforcement to avoid race conditions.

Manifest format: JSON manifest with fields: artifact_id, type (prompt/response/log/metric), sha256, created_at, retained_until, retention_policy_id, residency_regions, release_channel. Manifest must be canonicalized before signing.
Signing: use KMS/HSM via existing KMS integrations; support customer-managed keys for Private deployments. Store signature metadata (key id, signature algorithm) in audit log.
Export performance: for large tenants, export will use streaming tar creation and background chunked upload; provide pre-signed S3 URL or direct download depending on deployment.
Backwards compatibility: if older artifacts lack digest metadata, include 'digest_unavailable' flag and record in manifest; we will backfill digests as a follow-up.
Security: evidence bundles contain sensitive PII; default export access controlled by RBAC; require MFA for manual exports for enterprise tenants.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): implement anchor + eviction harmonization + manifest schema; run on Canary tenants with synthetic load; enable Evidence Assertion API in read-only mode.
Phase 2 (beta): enable export generation for select customers with NDAs; add KMS signing and Console preview for manifests; collect feedback on bundle usability.
Phase 3 (general): GA for Hosted and Dedicated; provide deployment guide and customer-managed key instructions for Private.

Rollback: disable Evidence Assertion API and mark historic bundles as unverifiable (audit event) if signing pipeline fails; rolling back anchor changes will require re-run of eviction job with new anchor parameters.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Eng, Security, and Console teams; agreed schema and canonicalization rules; Eng to prototype anchor job.
2026-03-05: Security completed KMS threat assessment; recommends customer-managed keys for Private; SRE to implement key rotation test harness.
2026-03-09: Prototype manifest returned canonical JSON and passed signing roundtrip against staging KMS; performance concern noted for >1M artifacts in window — Eng to add streaming tar pipeline.
2026-03-10: PM requested Console preview wireframes; design assigned to DES-60122 for compact manifest viewer.
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest canonicalization and digest checks.
Integration tests that simulate TTL changes and verify exported manifest assertions before and after anchor updates.
Load tests for export on synthetic 10M artifact tenant to characterize SLOs and costs.
Manual QA checklist for RBAC/MFA gating on exports and KMS key usage verification.
notes: This approach emphasizes 'time as the single source of truth' for retention decisions and gives auditors a cryptographically-signed snapshot of retention state. We should coordinate with Legal for export retention of evidence bundles themselves (how long we keep generated bundles).
